title: was told to post my game here for better feedback
author: Present_Reality_2197
selftext:
Game Title: Broken Dagger

Playable Link: [https://thetk421guy.itch.io/broken-dagger](https://thetk421guy.itch.io/broken-dagger)

isometric action game where you control and fight versions of yourself from across infinite realms.

gamepad is needed to play. (pic is from mobile but half the moves won’t work without gamepad)

i have been using different platforms to edit this including gemini, chatgpt and claude. so far claude is the best an has only been limited by usage when ive been working too much. i am getting the hang of adding functions and i am impressed it is working as well as it does. there are some features that could be explained better but i’m interested in some perspectives! thanks

replies.author: Ohgood9002
replies.body:
I feel the same way. These browser based vibe coded games are just prototypes. If people want serious feedback then they need to be serious about making a game on an actual engine and not some early 2000s browser game.

If you like your prototype, scale it up to and rebuild it on an engine

replies.author: Present_Reality_2197
replies.body: what would be a good plan for scaling? i feel like a lot of what the browser game is doing can be done in any engine. i have quite a bit of functions beyond what i understood before vibe coding this game but i might be able to understand more of working in the engine now. 7 or 8 years ago i was following game maker/unity tutorials and just felt like i was copying what the tutorial was making but it helped me learn a ton which helped me vibe code better.

replies.author: Ohgood9002
replies.body:
You can pretty much work the exact same way you have been, just have claude connect to your project through the terminal. Or use the codex desktop app and direct it to your project file. Then it will just pretty much act the exact same way, but it will be building the game directly in a GODOT project folder instead of a browser game.

There are some nice benefits of being able to manually move assets around, etc. All the stuff AI isn't good at yet. All the "polish". You have far more freedom with what the engine can output. 

Step 1 - Download GODOT (its free and open source)

Step 2 - Start GODOT and make your first project. Just name the folder, thats literally it. Stop there.

Step 3 - Direct Claude or Codex to the project folder.

Step 4 - Upload your old project to claude/codex and say "I really like my prototype. Help me rebuild my game in GODOT. Create and roadmap and system implementation plan to assist. I am a solo developer with not much experience. Explain the processes and terminology like I am 5 years old"

  
And then my favorite prompt for anything, but you want to ask this in Claude AI, not claude code. Claude AI is better at design. "Ask me 10 (20, 30. etc) questions to help me design and rebuild my game. Use those answers to craft a GDD (game design document) and implementation roadmap that we can work on together. Create .md files that i can drop into my project folder for Claude to use as instructions. "

After the project folder is set up and you have all your design and implementation documents in place you can then ask Claude AI (not code) "Write a Claude Code prompt for me to have claude code start building and creating my game. Give me a project audit afterwards to determine the next steps"

Claude is probably going to write the core systems first and wont care about assets for the first few steps. this is normal, eventually it'll start wanting to put down it's own placeholder assets to create a game scene

some final tips - Tell claude/codex to make all visible game assets... visible. It loves to hide assets in the runtime or not properly display them, making manual adjustment a pain later on when you need to move a UI window 3 pixels to the left. 

I've also found codex to be much much much better for this type of vibe coding. I recommend having Claude AI write the design and use codex to implement the design. I'll use claude code to run project audits and check code stability.

replies.author: Present_Reality_2197
replies.body: thank you so much for this. i will start this asap! this seems like a much better way to manage what i am doing because at this point the game is getting really big for just one html file i really appreciate this thoughtful response and your willingness to be helpful!

replies.author: Ohgood9002
replies.body:
If you can afford both claude code and codex you'll pretty much just want to use codex to vibecode build the game and Claude just to run audits. Claude will cleanup your code and project architecture so it's not all one gigantic script. It'll make your systems run cleaner as well. 

I'd ask claude AI to help you design some GDDs (game design documents) to assist claude/codex. Currently i have design documents for

AGENTS - A document that says "Claude, you're the designer, Codex you're the mechanic"

CLAUDE - The instructions for claude code to follow for your game design.

GDD - My full complete game design overview, each system broken down

IMPLEMENTATION\_STATUS - I gave claude and codex instructions to update this document with implementation progress so both claude and codex can stay on the same page when doing audits, etc. This gets updated alongside every change to the project. This also assists with keeping the other documents up to date and aligned with each other. Ask claude to keep a implementation log that the other AI agent can access. if using codex be specific and say "hey, i have another AI working on this project. create an implementation document so you guys can "talk" to each other"

ART LAYER SPECS - A document that has all the information for the art style and design tone for the game. 

  
LORE - The game lore

NARRATIVE DESIGN - This document has all my rules for narrative design and narrative tone. The tone of my game is satire in the vein of Douglas Addams/ The Hitchhikers Guide. This document makes any generated text fit the tone i've set for the rest of the dialog and scenes. Don't skip this, this gives your game more identity than you think. Pick a book/author you like to emulate their style. 

  
ROADMAP - The project roadmap, the plan. Claude/Codex won't get anywhere without a full roadmap. Make sure to include "gate points". Steps that you absolutely cannot start on unless the gate point steps have been cleared. I promise this will keep things on track and flowing. Just ask claude to make sure that you have gate points in your plan.

  
WORKFLOW - At some point i updated my workflow with more specific instructions and just added this. I probably could have re-written AGENTS as it serves the same purpose. 

  
I also have .md files for character relationship systems, map and event node systems, etc. i would recommend making a separate document for each core system. Is combat a system? Then one document for combat. Another document for trading and economy rules. Another document for inventory management, etc. 

Just say "Hey claude, lets design the inventory system. Ask me 10 questions to help design the inventory and write a .md that i can drop into the project folder for the AI agents to reference"

  
Be aware that you need to update your instructions for every document you add. the easiest way to do this is just add your document/replace the old one and say "Hey Codex, i added a new design document about inventory. Do an audit on my project and make sure all documentation aligns with the next file i provided. Update any necessary files"

  
sorry for the wall of text. I'm caffeinated and feeling helpful
